name: Kazakhstan

findings.summary: Kcell chose Ericsson as its 5G radio access partner for a seven-year deal to 2030, using single RAN integrated with existing 2G-4G, targeting coverage of at least half the country including Almaty and Shymkent.
findings.analyst_inference: RAN only; Kcell's core vendor not identified. Value undisclosed. Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. The other operators' (Kazakhtelecom/Tele2-Altel, Beeline) 5G RAN vendors were not identified in this pass.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovations and Aerospace Industry
findings.summary: The digital development ministry and Huawei Technologies Kazakhstan signed an ICT cooperation memorandum at Huawei's Shanghai headquarters, setting up a joint working group to propose digital-infrastructure modernisation for 2025-2030; no projects or values named.
findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding MOU, tier 1. DKNews is a Kazakh outlet; whether it is state-affiliated was not checked. Coded networks because 5G and network modernisation lead the stated scope; it also mentions cloud and AI.

findings.summary: Huawei Technologies Kazakhstan and operator Tele2/Altel signed a cooperation memorandum, according to a Kazakh business outlet headline; terms were not seen.
findings.analyst_inference: Search-result title only; fetch failed, so the memorandum's scope (RAN, core, AI) is unknown. Whether Huawei already supplies Tele2/Altel's radio network was not established; that would be the more important fact.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of AI and Digital Development; Samruk-Kazyna
findings.summary: During President Tokayev's July 2026 Shanghai visit Huawei signed a telecommunications agreement with the digital ministry and an equipment-and-technology purchase agreement with sovereign fund Samruk-Kazyna, among 70+ deals; no individual values disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded at tier 1 because neither agreement's content, value or layer is stated; the Samruk-Kazyna purchase agreement could be tier 3 if it is a binding procurement, but the equipment type is not known, so the layer is a guess. Single source. The visit coincided with WAICO's founding (global layer).

findings.summary: Chinese cable and network group Hengtong signed an agreement with Kazakhtelecom to develop a data-centre hub during the July 2026 Shanghai visit; no value, site or capacity reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the source does not say whether Hengtong would own/operate the hub, build it, or supply equipment. If Kazakhtelecom owns it the facility is domestic with Hengtong as builder or vendor. Single source; instrument read as tier 1.

findings.local_actor: Kazakhtelecom; Ministry of AI and Digital Development
findings.summary: US infrastructure firm Firebird signed a strategic cooperation agreement with the AI ministry and a binding term sheet with Kazakhtelecom for 'Data Center Valley' at Ekibastuz: two 125 MW AI data centres planned for 2027-28, about US$10bn announced.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: a term sheet and framework agreement, no financing or construction start reported. Pole us is a tentative reading from the Prime Minister's attribution of the US$10bn investment to Firebird; ownership/operation is not stated, and Kazakhtelecom could be co-owner. Nvidia is named as Firebird's partner but no chip order is identified. 300 MW of power available, 1 GW target.

findings.local_actor: JSC National Information Technologies (NIT); Alem.cloud national supercomputer centre
findings.summary: Kazakhstan launched its national supercomputer Alem.cloud at a digital ministry data centre: 496 Nvidia H200 GPUs in HPE Cray XD670 nodes with Intel Xeon CPUs, claimed up to 2 exaflops FP8; President Tokayev attended.
findings.analyst_inference: GPU count and node model come from the NIT project page; launch date from Interfax/ForkLog. Value and integrator not disclosed. Facility is state-owned (domestic) but the equipment controller for the silicon layer is US (Nvidia/HPE). Export licence for the H200s not seen.

findings.local_actor: Freedom Holding Corp.; Bilim Group; ministries of AI and Digital Development, Education, Science and Higher Education
findings.summary: Under OpenAI's Education for Countries programme, an OpenAI-Freedom Holding-Bilim Group agreement gives 165,000 free ChatGPT Edu licences to Kazakh teachers and university staff; activation via BilimClass began in a nationwide rollout in 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Agreements reached during Tokayev's November 2025 US visit; signatories are private (Freedom Holding sponsors, privately funded), with ministries as partners. Used through OpenAI's service, so pole us. Two opened S3 sources but no opened S1/S2, so not corroborated. Tier 3 for the signed licence agreement; actual activation numbers not reported.

findings.summary: ISSAI at Nazarbayev University built KazLLM, government-requested 8B and 70B models on Llama 3.1, trained on 8 Nvidia DGX H100 nodes; released December 2024 with a non-exclusive licence to Astana Hub and public weights.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 (built and released, but ISSAI says it knows of no current operational deployment). Weights held domestically, so pole domestic. AlemLLM (the Alem.ai model) was not researched; its base model is unknown.

findings.summary: Astana approved a 2025-2030 public-private partnership handing its city video-surveillance system to G42 subsidiary Presight, which funds 53bn tenge for about 22,000 cameras, 732 intersection units and a situation centre.
findings.analyst_inference: Presight is Emirati, so pole third. 53bn tenge not converted (no source-date rate seen). Camera counts differ between sources (10,000 new plus 8,000 integrated vs 22,000). Camera hardware vendor (Hikvision/Dahua or other) not identified; Kazakh firms to do 60% of work. Installation progress not confirmed.

findings.reversal_of: Sergek city video-surveillance PPP, Astana (Korkem Telecom consortium)
findings.summary: Astana's public-private partnership with Korkem Telecom for the domestic Sergek surveillance system expired on 13 March 2025 and was not renewed; management passed to Emirati firm Presight.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a reversal (non-renewal) of a domestic operational system; reason recorded as commercial because sources give only contract expiry, no security or political reason. Sergek continues in other Kazakh cities and is exported to Uzbekistan (not verified here).

power.null_reason: only AI-linked power evidence is the 300 MW available at Ekibastuz for Data Center Valley (captured in KAZ-006); no dedicated plant or utility filing found

research_gaps: Which vendors supply 5G/4G RAN and core for Kazakhtelecom/Tele2-Altel and Beeline (Veon)? Is Huawei an incumbent RAN supplier, and what does the October 2025 Huawei-Tele2/Altel memorandum cover?
Huawei-Samruk-Kazyna purchase agreement (July 2026): what equipment, value and binding status?
Hengtong-Kazakhtelecom data-centre hub: owner/operator, site, capacity, and whether Hengtong is builder, vendor or owner.
Data Center Valley (Ekibastuz): who owns and operates the facilities, financing close, construction start, chip supply and US export licences.
AlemLLM / Alem.ai model: base model and weight control; any government deployment of KazLLM.
Astana Presight system: camera hardware vendor and installation progress; Almaty and other cities' safe-city vendors (Hikvision/Dahua/Huawei) and current Sergek footprint.
Export licence for the 496 Nvidia H200s in Alem.cloud, and any further accelerator purchases (including Huawei Ascend).
